drivers.why_material: Catalyst trial (NCT06510816) primary endpoint is BCVA ≥15-letter loss (clinical), yet marketing asserts Phase 2 biomarker (photoreceptor preservation) will 'reproduce' in ARCHER II as a predictor of vision preservation. This positions a non-validated biomarker as the basis for expecting catalyst success.

Marketing claims ellipsoid zone structure is 'key to visual acuity' for the catalyst trial, but EZ is only a secondary endpoint in NCT06510816. Repeated emphasis on a non-validated biomarker as predictive of the primary clinical outcome suggests management is masking low confidence in the registered primary.

Direct claim that photoreceptor protection 'is responsible for visual acuity protection' in the context of the Phase 3 catalyst. This biomarker-to-clinical leap, repeated across multiple exhibits leading up to the catalyst, suggests management is pre-positioning a biomarker rationale to explain a potential primary endpoint miss.

Marketing emphasizes 'prevention of ellipsoid zone loss' as an 'objective secondary structural measure' when the registered primary is BCVA loss. This de-emphasis of the primary in favor of a secondary biomarker endpoint is a classic tell that the primary is expected to be weak.

analyst_note: EXCLUDE. Marketing systematically repositions a non-validated biomarker (photoreceptor/ellipsoid zone preservation) as predictive of the Phase 3 ARCHER II primary endpoint (BCVA ≥15-letter loss), despite EZ being registered only as secondary. Ten separate moderate-severity findings document this biomarker-to-clinical leap across exhibits from August 2024 through May 2026, with increasing intensity approaching the catalyst. One finding shows explicit de-emphasis of the primary in favor of the secondary structural measure. The pattern indicates management lacks confidence in the registered primary and is pre-positioning a biomarker narrative to explain a miss. The registry shows primary endpoint changes and completion slippage, consistent with trial execution stress. All cross-trial comparison findings (minor severity) are dismissed as standard competitive positioning and do not bear on catalyst-trial honesty.
